src_in: 0-12 s: H to He, core tightening (no text)
vo_text: Deep inside, the sun is fusing hydrogen into helium.
The net of the proton -proton chain is simple enough to say aloud.
Four hydrogen nuclei become one helium nucleus.
A little mass becomes energy and that energy is the light.
The radiation that leaves the surface takes eight minutes to reach you.
The energy was made long before that.
Here is the turn. Helium is not a second sort of hydrogen.
Each helium nucleus locks up more mass in fewer particles.
As the core fills with ash, fewer particles remain to hold the star up against
gravity. Pressure would fall unless something else rose.

vo_text: So the core contracts a little. It heats.
Hotter hydrogen fuses faster. Faster fusion releases more
energy and the star brightens. The sun brightens because it is
running down. The waste in the middle leaves the fire no choice but to burn harder.
That is the first payoff. The tank is not dimming as it empties.
